note: Both sets read the shared claims correctly: the 4° pitch limit, the 90 m force peak, the design and optimal TSR values, and the Prandtl tip-loss drop are all faithful to the text. Set B additionally captures the design-point blade pitch Θpitch = 0° and the optimal Θpitch = −1.0°, which are genuine engineering values stated in the same sentence and omitted by Set A. Since Set A shows all of its claims and lacks these pitch values, B is the more complete and equally accurate set.
remarks: Both sets state the force peak as exactly 90 m while the text says 'approximately 90 m'; minor, but the approximation qualifier is dropped. The 'optimal' TSR/pitch pair is described via the CP and CT curves in Figure 3-2, so 'maximum CP' as a condition is a reasonable but slightly simplified gloss.
